title: Website as therapy
description: I've never been to therapy but I've heard it's awesome. Honestly, the idea of having someone listening to me yapping about all my problems sounds amazing, but for now I'm letting my friends fulfill that roll. I've always enjoyed it when friends have told me about their therapy, though, especially when they have to do therapy homework. One of the most common therapy homeworks I've heard about is documenting your life! Keeping a diary and writing down your feelings.

Turns out, I've been doing that for 10 years already! On the 14th of August 2016 I randomly decided to start a daily diary and it's still going today. It's literally just a spreadsheet with a date and like one or two sentences about what I did that day. I learned from previous attempts that writing feelings down is costly and difficult, so factual records were the way to go: so much easier.

At several points I've left it over a week and have had to remember all the things I did over the past week (sometimes really hard) and fill it in nachträglich, but I always end up doing it because of the sunken costs thing. It would just be a massive shame to stop now I've made it this far. It's very easy to just fill in the gaps when it's just what I did that day, so I've been able to keep it all full. Don't get me wrong, sometimes I go for a longer one as well, but sometimes it's just something like 'Sports was very chill. Was zonked so had an early night'.

Doing this has been amazing for so many unforeseen reasons! First, I can remember what I did on any given day. I can look back at any day in the past 10 years and be like, oh yeah I remember that day! All the memories and feelings relating to it come flooding back. It really helps me feel like my life isn't slipping away from me. You know how it feels like time gets faster as you get older? Doing this really helps combat that feeling, because you can literally see all the things you did. Rereading years feels like reliving them. It doesn't feel like I've wasted my life.

It also forces me to reflect on my days and sometimes reconsider them. Writing the diary entry for bad days a few days later makes me realise that the day maybe wasn't as bad as I thought it was. So I totally get why therapists say to document things. I highly, highly recommend doing it too!

I also just have an affinity for documenting things. I mean, look at this website. I get to document all the media I consume, write down my thoughts and feelings on almost anything. These newsletters are opinions on larger topics and it just feels good to put them down on paper. I wonder if my last one about AI will still hold up in one year. Feels good knowing I can go back and read it.

Anyway, thanks for reading this one. No major updates to the site recently, but I did change the recommended RSS feed app for the newsletter. Feedly apparently pivoted to AI cybersecurity. My real recommendation is to vibe-code your own RSS reader but that's pretty next-level I guess (that's my plan for the weekend at least).

entries.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
description: What an absolute dream. I'm still reeling from the fact that this exists! The original Ocarina of Time was such a formative part of my life, reliving it in full HD is almost surreal. I remember playing it as an 8 year old and being terrified of the skeletons in Hyrule Field, and had to get my brothers to do it for me. Then later in life I would get further and become terrified of the Redeads (still scary to this day) and get my brothers to do the Shadow Temple for me. And then in later years I would come back and beat it all myself, and Majora's Mask too (even scarier), and learning about speedrunning, cheats, secrets and lore. By the time I was an adult, I had played the game through at least 15 times and knew everything about it. The soundtrack stayed with me forever, and what can I say? It's just a perfect little childhood nostalgic game.

This remake pays so much respect to it, so much so that I would say it really lives up to the original. They've smoothed out some of the rougher parts but not in a way that significantly changes how the game plays, and they added lots of exciting new things, also in a way which respects the original, like the new Castle Town, or the sneaking past the guards section. I loved all the changes, honestly! When I played through the Water Temple, I realised that the key underneath the block in the central room had been removed and I thought to myself, that makes sense, honestly. Turns out they took out two keys and I didn't notice! Unlike back then, they did a lot of play testing here I think. Also, the Water Temple was and remains the best temple in terms of gameplay. In terms of VIBES, the prize for best temple of course has to go to the unforgettable Forest Temple, which they knocked out of the park in this game. It looks stunning with the new stained-glass windows and colours. Love it so much.

There are new cutscenes as well! Little pieces of reworked dialogue really serve to make more sense of the otherwise nonsensical story. Things like saying explicitly that Ganondorf was here and did something to Jabu-Jabu, or explaining that Rauru pulled the sages into the Sacred Realm makes a lot of sense and I totally approve. The best one is the amazing scene where you pull the Master Sword. It adds that missing context, and also just goes so hard. Ganondorf rocks in this game.

I love the updated soundtrack, it's very faithful to the original but just sounds more lush and orchestral. I love it. I love the new night-time versions, and in general I love that the day-night cycle continues no matter where you are. And the characters! They all look so good. Impa has the best glow-up for sure, but I also enjoy Zelda and Ganondorf's new looks, and I was totally gagged by Nabooru of the Gerudo. Stunning.

The game is easy. Don't go into this expecting anything challenging, but that makes it accessible. Unlike Breath of the Wild, I think Nintendo wanted this to be a hit with as many people as possible, and having an easy game (with great vibes) is a nice way to be accessible for everyone. For me, who already knows everything about the game, it was a case of me just sailing through. For Jack, who I watched play for the first time, they had to use their brain a bit, but the game provides enough signposts to show them where they can go next.

I also appreciate that they kept it weird. All the weird, unexplained shit from the original is still all there because why the fuck not. Twinrova, two elderly witches, fuse into a hot young woman for the Spirit Temple boss, which is really weird if you think about it. King Zora still inches to the left painfully slowly, and this time the camera really shows it off in all its glory. Love it. It keeps in the time paradox with the Song of Storms because why not. The cow in death mountain is still stuck in a hole.
Anyway, I am delighted that this game exists, I recommend it to everyone, and I can't wait for Majora's Mask.

entries.title: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort
description: Jack got this with their Switch 2 and we tried a few of the games. Some of them? Total bullshit. Thumb wrestling is totally dumb and random. I liked the volleyball and golf though. The highlight was flying the plane over Wuhu Island though. It felt like good old Pilotwings 3DS times, although I think that game is better. I'm told this sports game is a banger but I've yet to see its true magic.

entries.title: Titanium Court
description: Nowadays it's hard to describe games without mentioning other games, but this one truly is unique. It's a story about a person waking up being told she is the queen of the castle, and that the castle is at war, and all her fairy subjects are all super weird and clueless and dripfeeding her information (but also hiding it from her) about what's actually going on. It's all clearly a metaphor for other things, and as you go to war in the game and do a bunch of things, you'll have a nagging sensation that your actions have consequences. The writing is really good and really kooky, and is ultimately what kept me going.

The gameplay is a match-3 puzzle situation to set up a board, then you have to fight your opponents castles. It's hard to describe but pretty tactical. It is another fucking roguelike though, goddamn. Wild shit happens each and every run though, so it's good. The presentation of the game is also really cool - it's all in this magenta-cyan-yellow colour pallette which is kinda giving trans. I like how it looks a lot.

I admit, I haven't beaten the game yet. I have four keys but it doesn't feel right to finish the game until I do more stuff. However, I've decided to take a break from it because there's clearly still lots to do, and it's getting quite difficult so I've started losing runs which is frustrating.

entries.title: La Bola Negra
description: Gorgeous, sweeping epic all about gay romance during the Spanish civil war. It covers loads of grounds and has many themes. Honestly I think it's the kind of film that you need to see twice. I really liked it.

entries.title: Mario Kart DS
description: Huge drop on the app! These are some certified childhood bangers right here. I love that special DS vibe that comes with this soundtrack. I feel it shares a lot in common with the Gamecube version. The Title and Menu themes are just so good. Huge vibes! I feel like 'Delfino Square' was the blueprint for timeless bangers like Coconut Mall and Daisy Circuit. 'Waluigi Pinball' is, as we all know, a huge bop that will stay with all of us forever. This 'Rainbow Road' is just everything.
The retro tracks are never as good as the originals, but ironically I heard a lot of this music for the first time here. So I owe a lot to this game really.
entries.metadata: Platform: DS, for a list of favourite tracks, please visit the nintendo soundtracks page!

entries.title: Pikmin Bloom
description: Damn, they're doing mobile games now! The Nintendo Music App continues to surprise us. Luckily, this soundtrack provides some more material for my 'pikmin vibes' playlist. It borrows a lot from 'Hey! Pikmin' on the 3DS, a game which isn't good, but whose soundtrack has some really great top-tier Pikmin music. So I don't think I'll ever play this boring ass game but I appreciate some of these music tracks for sure.
That being said, this soundtrack does not make for a good listening experience. A lot of the tracks sound like corporate music.
entries.metadata: Platform: Mobile, for a list of favourite tracks, please visit the nintendo soundtracks page!

entries.title: The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time
description: Omigosh! This game is everything and they really smashed it with this soundtrack. Holy shit! They took the timeless original and with great respect added so much to it. Lush string sections, whimsical instruments, or indeed the original weird synth sounds. For now, we just have these 8 tracks but holy god damn they are amazing. The 'Title Theme' is everything. Everything and more. It's so melancholic and dramatic and perfect. 'Kokiri Forest', 'Market' and 'Kakariko Village' are all classics and so gorgeous. I love how they add more instrumentation on the second loop, similar to how the Link's Awakening remake did it. There's also 'Hyrule Field' which includes all the variations, resulting in a whopping 9 minutes of bombastic nonsense, which admittedly doesn't make for a good listening experience. I love 'Zora's Domain' so much and holy god damn they knocked 'Gerudo Valley' out of the park. They somehow made it into even more of a banger. Is the percussion slightly different? I danced around my house the first time I heard it.
Please do go listen to the rest of the soundtrack on youtube! There's so much more to discover! Day/Night themes, the more ambient tracks, (personal favourite Forest Temple).
entries.metadata: Platform: Switch 2, for a list of favourite tracks, please visit the nintendo soundtracks page!

entries.title: Pokémon Legends: ZA
description: I groaned when this popped up in the app, but my friend Oscar calmed me down and said don't worry, this soundtrack is actually full of bangers and he's right! It turns out a youtuber I used to follow, insaneintherain, is all over this soundtrack and you can hear it. It's really giving jazz fusion. Listening to it was a bit funny because these Gen 6 tracks I really associate with the Kalos stage from smash but here they are here in a new, exciting form. Doesn't make me want to play the game though.
entries.metadata: Platform: Switch, for a list of favourite tracks, please visit the nintendo soundtracks page!

entries.title: Jessie Ware
description: Wow, this is up there with CMAT as one of my favourite concerts ever! She was amazing. I loved her dancers, they were so camp and ridiculous, and the crowd was great. She played all the best songs from her disco era, and really blew us all away honestly. She's such an amazing singer. So many props as well!
